info.name: Campus Errand - Order & Credit Service Flows
info.description:
AI Assistance Disclosure:
Tool: Codex (model: GPT-6), date: 2026-10-22
Scope: Generated order/credit HTTP flow, validation, authorization, state matrix, concurrency, ledger and notification assertions from existing service implementations.
Author review: <to be completed by huangjiaxi1111>

Run the whole collection sequentially with one iteration. No environment is required. Configure oc* URL/credential variables; defaults call services directly like postman_collection.json. To exercise gateway routing, set all five service URL variables to http://localhost. Requires all services, migrated databases, RabbitMQ and all three Debezium connectors. Setup creates four unique STUDENT accounts plus one dedicated supplier using the seeded admin. Do not run against production. Test accounts, orders, wallets and ledger remain for inspection; the supplier is soft-deactivated at the end. A new run creates independent fixtures. Do not run setup twice within the same run or run dependent folders alone.

HTTP 202 is a PENDING receipt, not a successful reservation. Bounded polls wait for both reservation outcome and wallet/ledger convergence. Failed prerequisites stop the run. Successful HTTP actions are not event replays: repeats must conflict and must not charge/refund twice. No escrow mutation HTTP routes exist (404). Default run covers deterministic HTTP cases. PENDING while Credit is offline, Supplier outage and real 30-minute expiry folders are opt-in; read order_credit_README.md before enabling them. HTTP cannot prove DLQ, event replay fingerprints, database rollback injection, WebSocket delivery or every possible interleaving. The README maps those to existing lower-level tests and manual checks. No finite collection can exhaust every possible input or schedule.

Source traceability: issue #21 (F4.6, F4.6.1, F4.6.1.1, F4.6.1.2, F4.6.2) and #60; HTTP checks demonstrate observable event effects, not full completion of broker/rollback criteria. Current implementation emits credit reservation outcomes; completion/refund outcomes are not separate public HTTP resources.
